name: Sanctions

subjectOf.text: Certification requirements that compel directors and officers to certify compliance with a CIA's provisions lower the procedural and enforcement hurdles for pursuing increased sanctions against noncompliant companies.
subjectOf.abstract: Certification requirements in CIAs, which require directors and officers to certify compliance with the CIA's provisions, can lower procedural and enforcement hurdles.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: CIAs containing board and officer certification requirements

subjectOf.text: At the pre charging stage the government typically holds extraordinary bargaining power, which lets it extract fines and sanctions comparable to those following a criminal conviction while avoiding the risk and cost of trial.
subjectOf.abstract: The government typically has extraordinary bargaining power at the pre-charging stage, enabling it to extract fines and sanctions similar to those from a criminal conviction69 without the risk and cost of a trial.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Timothy Lacine, The Effect of Deferred and Non-Prosecution Agreements on Corporate Governance Evidence from 1993-20 (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2486570
scope_conditions: applies at the pre charging stage

subjectOf.text: Reputational penalties for non-performance in a DAO are entirely free from racial implications because token holders are unlikely to even know each other.
subjectOf.abstract: Crucially, non- performance reputational penalties are entirely free from racial implications as the token holders are unlikely to even know each other.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Blockchain Technology and Race in Corporate America (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3071378
